clue.text: To start an argument deliberately, choose a soppy gift full of hearts

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: something full of a thing has it inside, so one letter goes within the word before
soppy suggests something soft and mushy, losing its shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A sentimental Valentine's present goes down badly and starts a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts looks like romantic decoration for the soppy gift; in cards it is the abbreviation that goes inside before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick a fight is the idiom for provoking a quarrel on purpose.

clue.text: View shown in brochure American dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is left out, so those letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a prospectus is a brochure describing a school or company
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A holiday brochure shows a scenic view, with the American edition dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide outlook or vista, as in a fine prospect over the valley.

clue.text: Cross Copper Belt, ultimately

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of belt

explanation.surface: Instructions for crossing the Copper Belt, the mining region of Zambia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Copper Belt is a real mining region in central Africa, which disguises the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut across a path is to cross it, as one line cuts another.

clue.text: Where juvenile delinquents were once taken in official coach?

definitions.text: Where juvenile delinquents were once taken

parts.note: something official has been approved
to coach is to school or train

explanation.surface: Young offenders are driven off to their institution in an official bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach looks like a vehicle carrying the delinquents, but it is the verb meaning train.
explanation.definitionFit: Approved schools were British residential institutions for young offenders, abolished in 1969.

clue.text: Have a look at cricket perhaps, around start of play

indicators.note: around means wrapping about, so the first word encloses the next letter

parts.note: a cricket is one example of an insect, signalled by perhaps

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of play

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch some cricket around the time play starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the chirping insect, not the bat-and-ball game the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it closely, to look it over.

clue.text: Keen to goad fiery person

parts.note: hot on something means keen on it
to spur is to goad or urge on

explanation.surface: Someone eager to provoke a hot-tempered person.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotspur was the nickname of Harry Percy, the impetuous rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, hot-headed person, after Shakespeare's fiery Harry Percy.

clue.text: Loot is produced by foremost of stage-managers, habitual joker

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of stage-managers
a wag is someone who habitually makes jokes

explanation.surface: Backstage, a theatre's practical joker turns out to be a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods, the haul of a burglar.

clue.text: Worried less about a number of baseball games

indicators.note: about here means turned around and moved about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan frets less about how many games of baseball are left.
explanation.definitionFit: The World Series is the championship of American baseball, a best-of-seven set of games.

clue.text: 'Splendid gathering in high spirits around LA' ('Times')

indicators.note: around means enclosing, so the word for high spirits wraps the next pieces

parts.note: gay in its older sense of merry, cheerful
taken as written
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper quote describing a glittering, cheerful party in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: LA and Times together suggest the Los Angeles Times newspaper; X is the times sign in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a brilliant assembly of notable people, as in a galaxy of stars.

clue.text: Illegal practice involving still and gin allies drunk

parts.note: inert means motionless, still

indicators.note: drunk words stagger about out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Running an illicit distillery and getting gin-sodden companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Still looks like the distilling apparatus, fitting the gin; it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia selling is sending unrequested goods and demanding payment unless returned, banned in Britain.

clue.text: Fellow leaving centre holding toy sea creature

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so the shortened word surrounds another
leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: the focus is the centre of attention
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a spinning top is a toy

explanation.surface: A man walks out of a play centre carrying a toy octopus.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F from FOCUS leaves OCUS, which then holds TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The octopus is an eight-armed marine mollusc.

clue.text: Twirl endlessly round object? This part of a plant can

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the shortened word goes about the next one
without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: trill in an old sense means to twirl or turn round
an end is an aim or object, as in to that end

explanation.surface: A climbing shoot twirling around whatever it touches.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the plant part too: it really can twirl round an object. Trill's old meaning of twirl is rare but in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot by which a climbing plant clings to supports.

clue.text: Father to sit holding ring for baby

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the second word encloses a letter

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A father sits for a portrait holding a ring meant for the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Papoose is a word, from Algonquian, for a young Native American child.

clue.text: Aurora borealis as seen from hilltop — rag's spread

indicators.note: spread out means scattered about, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watching the northern lights from a hill, with a newspaper spread out.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is slang for a newspaper, which the surface lays open on the hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis is the display of northern polar lights caused by solar particles.

clue.text: Airborne soldier comes into quayside, reportedly — there's a contradiction here!

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the word's sound counts, not spelling

parts.note: docks are a quayside; the spelling is changed to fit

explanation.surface: A paratrooper landing on the dockside makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: A paratrooper arriving by sea is itself odd, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement or situation that seems self-contradictory.

clue.text: Excitedly circles lot, to me a much sought-after object

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitated movement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: At an auction someone eagerly rings a lot in the catalogue, the one they covet.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector's item is a thing valued and hunted by collectors.

clue.text: Unique team? Daughter is biased

parts.note: one, as in one of a kind, means unique
a side is a team
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A sports commentator calls a team unique while a daughter thinks it partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one-sided favours one party unfairly, so it is partial.

clue.text: Inhabits floors, for a change efficiently arranged

indicators.note: a change of order is wanted, so the letters must be shifted around

parts.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lives on different storeys for variety, keeping everything neat.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is nautical: Bristol's ships were famously well kept, hence shipshape and Bristol fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol fashion means in good order, as in shipshape and Bristol fashion, from the city's tidy port.

clue.text: Figure in old trick involving label

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: involving means enclosing within, so the trick word surrounds the label word

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A dodgy figure caught up in a mislabelling scam.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a plane figure with eight sides.

clue.text: Plant releases one ahead of article

parts.note: to free is to release
I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A factory puts out a single product before a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant of the iris family from southern Africa.

clue.text: Never mind housing for despicable people!

indicators.note: housing means giving shelter inside, so the answer sits within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry: forget about giving homes to such dreadful people!
explanation.definitionFit: Vermin is used contemptuously for people regarded as loathsome, like pests.

clue.text: Descriptive term, extremely elegant, used about religious article

indicators.note: used about means placed around, so the ends enclose what follows
extremely refers to the extremes, so only the two end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of elegant
pi is informal for pious, religious
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A neat word for a stylish item used in worship.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an adjective or phrase characterising someone, such as the Great.

clue.text: Recruits strangely silent about closure of barracks

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word goes around the next letter
strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a closure is an ending, so only the final letter counts

parts.note: the last letter of barracks

explanation.surface: New soldiers are oddly quiet as the barracks shuts down.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to take on recruits for the forces, so it means recruits as a verb.

clue.text: Game John dealt with in periodical

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the rearranged name goes within the other word

parts.note: a mag is a periodical magazine

indicators.note: dealt with suggests cards being dealt out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine article about how John handled a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Dealt fits the game's surface, since mah jong tiles are dealt out like cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah jong is a Chinese tile game for four players.

clue.text: Forward (including gratuity) the minister's wages

indicators.note: including means taking inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: to forward a letter is to send it on
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass on a clergyman's pay with a little extra added.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is the fixed salary paid to a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Nobleman, for the most part getting attention

indicators.note: the most part is nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A lord mostly gets people listening to him.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone an ear is to give them attention, to listen.

clue.text: Reportedly recognises beak

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: to recognise someone is to know them

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that the bird identifies its own bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is slang for a person's nose, especially a large hooked one.

clue.text: Put in jeopardy as grenade exploded by border

parts.note: an end is a limit or boundary

indicators.note: something exploded is blown into pieces, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lives are put at risk when a bomb goes off by the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangered means exposed to danger or threatened.
